enhanced.fullText:
The Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), codified at 5 U.S.C. § 552, establishes the public's statutory right to access federal agency records, including those maintained by federally operated educational institutions and federal agencies overseeing higher education. While FOIA primarily applies to federal agencies, many state universities operate under parallel state freedom of information laws that mirror FOIA's framework.

Under 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(3), any person may request access to agency records without demonstrating a need or interest. Public universities must respond within 20 business days per 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(A)(i), though this may be extended by 10 additional days under exceptional circumstances as defined in 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(B).

FOIA establishes nine exemptions under 5 U.S.C. § 552(b), including classified information (Exemption 1), personnel records (Exemption 6), and investigatory records (Exemption 7). Higher education institutions must carefully balance FOIA obligations with Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) requirements under 20 U.S.C. § 1232g, as student education records may be protected from disclosure.

The FOIA Improvement Act of 2016 (Pub. L. 114-185) mandated proactive disclosure requirements and established a presumption of openness. Institutions must maintain electronic reading rooms per 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(2) and provide records in requested formats when readily reproducible.

Enforcement mechanisms include administrative appeals under 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(A)(i)(III)(aa) and federal court jurisdiction per 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(B). Courts may assess attorney fees against institutions for arbitrary or capricious withholding. The Office of Government Information Services (OGIS) provides mediation services under 5 U.S.C. § 552(h).

Institutions must designate FOIA officers, establish processing procedures, and maintain comprehensive record systems. Fee structures follow 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(4)(A), with different categories for commercial requesters, educational institutions, and media. Annual FOIA reports must be submitted to the Department of Justice per 5 U.S.C. § 552(e), detailing processing statistics, response times, and backlogs.
enhanced.summary: FOIA requires public universities to provide timely access to institutional records upon request, with specific exemptions for protected information. Institutions must respond within 20 business days, maintain electronic reading rooms, and balance transparency with FERPA privacy requirements.
enhanced.requirements:
## Record Access and Response
- Respond to FOIA requests within 20 business days per 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(A)(i)
- Designate official FOIA officers and establish processing procedures
- Provide records in requested electronic formats when readily reproducible
- Apply appropriate fee schedules based on requester categories

## Electronic Reading Room Maintenance
- Maintain publicly accessible electronic repositories per 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(2)
- Post frequently requested records and final agency decisions
- Update reading rooms with proactively disclosed information

## Privacy Protection and Exemptions
- Review records for applicable FOIA exemptions under 5 U.S.C. § 552(b)
- Coordinate with FERPA compliance to protect student education records
- Implement redaction procedures for partially exempt documents

## Administrative Procedures
- Establish internal appeal processes for denied requests
- Document exemption justifications and legal authority
- Train staff on FOIA processing requirements and deadlines
enhanced.reportingRequirements: Annual FOIA reports must be submitted to the Department of Justice by March 1st each year per 5 U.S.C. § 552(e), including processing statistics, response times, backlog data, and exemption usage. Quarterly backlog reports required for institutions with backlogs exceeding 1,000 requests.
